tagline: Self-hosted PHP web server that streams your own music and video library to browsers and apps.
description: Ampache serves an existing audio and video collection over the web. It reads metadata from the tags embedded in your files, or from file names, and presents the library in a browser interface and through an API that many third-party clients use. It does not organise files for you: the project says it assumes you already keep your collection in order. You run it on a web server (Apache is the most tested, nginx and lighttpd also work) with PHP, the required PHP modules, MySQL or MariaDB, and Node.js to build the front-end assets. A Docker image is published as well. The newest mainline, Ampache 8, requires PHP 8.5 or later, and the README recommends the release7 branch as the most stable line. A new opt-in Jellyfin-compatible API lets some Jellyfin client apps browse and stream the library. It is licensed AGPL-3.0. The closest paid comparison is Spotify Premium, but only for music you already own: there is no catalogue of licensed tracks. It suits people who already keep ripped or purchased music and want to reach it from a phone or browser without handing the files to a third party.
strengths: Streams both audio and video from your own files to a browser or through its API
Offers an opt-in Jellyfin-compatible API so clients such as Finamp or Symfonium can connect
Runs on Apache, nginx, lighttpd or IIS, with a published Docker image
Optional LDAP authentication and UPnP support
Has a documented public API with examples, used by third-party clients
limits: No music catalogue: it only serves files you already own, so it cannot replace Spotify's licensed library
It is not a media organiser; clean tags or file names are needed for good metadata
Needs MySQL or MariaDB, PHP with many modules and Node.js to build front-end assets, which is a heavier stack than a single binary
Ampache 8 needs PHP 8.5 or newer, and the stable recommendation is the older release7 branch
bestFor: A music collector with a tidy library of owned files and a home server who wants streaming to phone and browser without a subscription.
